To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the gut microbiota metabolizes choline and carnitine to form TMA, which is further oxidized by FMO3 to form TMAO.
TMAO and FMO3 are involved in the regulation of plasma lipid levels and atherogenesis.
TMAO is a link among diet, gut microbiota, liver and intestine cholesterol homeostasis and HDLC function.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the molecular pathways by FMO3 and TMAO that are involved in the regulation of plasma lipid metabolism and atherosclerosis.
the identification and characterization of novel molecular mechanisms by which TMA/TMA and their metabolite TMAO promote atherothrombosis and dyslipidemia.
the molecular mechanisms by which TMA/TMA-Oxide formation affects the risk of atherosclerosis.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the interplay among the diet, gut microbiota, and host genetics, including FMO3, is a key determinant for plasma TMAO levels.
TMAO, as well as its precursor TMA, are proatherogenic and that FMO3 plays a key role in this process.
TMAO is a marker of CVD risk, but the causal role of this compound in atherothrombosis is not fully established and the mechanisms by which it exerts its effects are still unclear.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
gut microbiota-derived TMAO and the FMO3 gene are important players in the regulation of plasma lipid levels and the risk for atherothrombosis.
gut microbiota, diet, and FMO3 are key determinants of plasma TMAO levels, which may affect the risk of CVD.
the gut microbiota, through TMAO, is an important regulator of cholesterol metabolism and that TMAO is a potential therapeutic target to prevent atherosclerosis.
The main takeaway from our work is that
gut microbiota, FMO3 and TMAO play a role in cholesterol homeostasis.
the TMAO plasma level is determined by the diet, gut microbiota composition and FMO3 genotype and that the gut microbiota composition may be manipulated in order to improve the plasma TMAO level.
TMAO and FMO3 are important players in the gut-liver-lipid axis.
